## What The Business Is

AppLovin is a technology/software company focused on AI-driven performance marketing. It provides software and AI tools that help businesses “reach, monetize and grow” audiences, with a core historical base in mobile gaming and an expanding “consumer” advertiser vertical such as e-commerce and lead-generation advertisers. ([s21.q4cdn.com](https://s21.q4cdn.com/165405286/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/1Q26-Earnings-Press-Release.pdf))

## What It Does

The company’s main platform matches advertisers with users across mobile game inventory using its Axon AI recommendation system. In late June 2026, AppLovin opened its self-serve ad platform to all advertisers, rebranding the advertiser-facing product from Axon to **AppLovin Ads**, while retaining **Axon** as the name of the AI recommendation engine; PocketGamer reported the platform reaches more than 1 billion daily active users through mobile gaming inventory. ([pocketgamer.biz](https://www.pocketgamer.biz/applovin-opens-self-serve-advertising-platform-to-all-advertisers/)) Management said on the May 6, 2026 call that the platform had been closed for 14 years and that public access, AI creative tools, and agent-compatible infrastructure were intended to let advertisers onboard, generate ads, and scale campaigns with minimal human support.

## Recent Highlights (Positive)

AppLovin reported a very strong Q1 2026: revenue of **$1.842 billion**, up **59% YoY**; net income of **$1.206 billion**, up **109% YoY**; adjusted EBITDA of **$1.557 billion**, up **66% YoY**; and an **85% adjusted EBITDA margin**. It also generated about **$1.3 billion** of operating cash flow and free cash flow, and repurchased/withheld **2.2 million shares** for **$1.0 billion** during the quarter. ([s21.q4cdn.com](https://s21.q4cdn.com/165405286/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/1Q26-Earnings-Press-Release.pdf)) Management guided Q2 2026 revenue to **$1.915–$1.945 billion** and adjusted EBITDA to **$1.615–$1.645 billion**, implying continued high growth and margins in the mid-80% range. ([s21.q4cdn.com](https://s21.q4cdn.com/165405286/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/1Q26-Earnings-Press-Release.pdf)) Operationally, management highlighted continued strength in gaming, accelerating consumer-advertiser spend, a material model improvement late in Q1, April consumer spend above prior Q4 peaks, and the June public launch as a major expansion of the addressable advertiser base.

## Recent Highlights (Negative)

Key risks and controversies remain visible. AppLovin’s own Q1 release flags risks around forecasting, scaling the business to support new users, competition in advertising, macro conditions, and adapting to emerging technologies/business models. ([s21.q4cdn.com](https://s21.q4cdn.com/165405286/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/1Q26-Earnings-Press-Release.pdf)) Short-seller and compliance-related overhangs have also persisted: recent coverage noted AppLovin pushing back against a CapitalWatch report it called defamatory, while prior reports and investor investigations have alleged issues including money-laundering links, ad-tech compliance, or data-practice concerns; these are allegations, and AppLovin has disputed at least some claims. ([marketspy.com](https://www.marketspy.com/news/applovin-pushes-back-against-short-seller-calls-capitalwatch-report-defamatory-and-demands-immediate-retraction?utm_source=openai)) Market sentiment has been mixed despite operating results: Zacks reported on July 7, 2026 that the stock was down roughly **19% year to date**, citing investor caution around valuation and macro uncertainty. ([zacks.com](https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2949707/is-applovins-19-year-to-date-pullback-a-buying-opportunity?utm_source=openai)) There is also execution and key-person transition risk: AppLovin announced that CTO Basil Shikin would step down July 1, 2026 and move to Distinguished Engineer, with Giovanni Ge becoming CTO; Chief Administrative & Legal Officer Victoria Valenzuela is set to retire August 1, 2026, with Corina Cacovean succeeding her as Chief Legal Officer. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1751008/000175100826000014/exhibit991-pressreleasexsu.htm?utm_source=openai))

## Bull Case
- Q1 2026 revenue +59% YoY, net income +109%, 85% adj. EBITDA margins, and ~$1.3B quarterly FCF show a compounding, capital-light model.
- The June 2026 self-serve launch (AppLovin Ads) opens the platform beyond gaming to all advertisers after 14 years closed — a major TAM expansion just beginning to monetize.
- Consumer-vertical spend is accelerating (April above prior Q4 peaks), and a material Axon model improvement landed late in Q1.
- Aggressive buybacks ($1.0B in Q1) shrink share count, amplifying per-share value.
- If FCF grows 55–60% over 12 months (~$6.9–7.1B) and the market holds the current ~40x EV/FCF, EV could approach $275B+.

## Bear Case
- Stock already down ~19% YTD despite strong results — the market is compressing the multiple on valuation and macro concerns.
- Growth is decelerating: FCF grew 119% then 75% YoY; extrapolating further deceleration suggests 35–45% forward growth, not 60%+.
- Short-seller allegations (compliance, data practices) remain an overhang, plus key-person transitions (CTO, Chief Legal Officer).
- Self-serve opening invites competitive response and execution/scaling risk with a new advertiser base.
- If forward FCF is only ~$5.8B and the multiple compresses to ~25x, EV would be ~$145B — meaningful downside.

## Logic
- **Forward FCF:** TTM FCF is $4,430.8M. Growth decelerated from ~119% to ~75% YoY; guidance and the self-serve launch support continued strength but at a moderating pace. I assume ~45% forward FCF growth → **~$6,400M** forward FCF.
- **Applied multiple:** Current EV/FCF is ~40x (EV $178,125M / $4,430.8M TTM FCF). Given decelerating growth, YTD multiple compression sentiment, and short-seller overhangs — offset by TAM expansion — I apply a modestly compressed **31x** forward EV/FCF.
- **EV:** 6,400 × 31 = **$198,400M**.
- **EV → Market cap bridge:** Current EV − market cap gap = 178,125 − 177,369.6 = $755.4M. Forward market cap = 198,400 − 755.4 = **~$197,645M**.

- Growth deceleration is likely as comps get harder; scaling self-serve to non-gaming advertisers is unproven at scale, and competition (Meta, Google) is intense.

- Forward FCF can exceed the base case if Q1’s ~$1.3B FCF run-rate scales with Q2 guidance and the public AppLovin Ads launch broadens advertiser demand.
- A bull case could justify ~$6.8B–$7.2B forward FCF.
- Applying a premium 42x–45x EV/FCF multiple, near the current/1-year valuation range, implies roughly $290B–$320B EV and ~$289B–$319B market cap after the EV-to-market-cap bridge.

## Bear Case
- Risks include valuation compression, advertiser concentration/execution risk, compliance/short-seller overhangs, leadership transition, and the possibility that consumer advertiser growth normalizes.
- A bear case could put forward FCF closer to ~$5.0B–$5.3B.
- Applying a lower 25x–28x EV/FCF multiple, closer to a derated software/ad-tech profile, implies roughly $125B–$148B EV and ~$124B–$147B market cap.

## Logic
- Current TTM FCF: **$4,430.8M**.
- Q1 2026 FCF was about **$1.3B**, or a ~$5.2B annualized run-rate, and Q2 guidance implies continued revenue/EBITDA growth.
- I estimate **12-month forward FCF of $6,000M**, representing about **35% growth** from current TTM FCF.
- Current EV/FCF is approximately **40.2x** based on $178,125M EV / $4,430.8M FCF.
- I apply a **35.0x EV/FCF multiple**, below the current multiple to reflect valuation, controversy, and execution risk, but above the 3-year average yield-implied multiple given exceptional growth and margins.
- Forward EV = **$6,000M × 35.0 = $210,000M**.
- Current EV minus market cap gap = **$178,125.0M - $177,369.6M = $755.4M**.
- Forward market cap = **$210,000M - $755.4M = $209,244.6M**.

## Bull Case
AppLovin's June 2026 public launch of its self-serve ad platform opens a previously closed ecosystem to all advertisers, dramatically expanding the addressable market beyond mobile gaming into e-commerce and lead-gen. Q1 2026 results (revenue +59% YoY, FCF ~$1.3B in a single quarter, 85% EBITDA margins) demonstrate the operating leverage of the model. If consumer-advertiser spend continues accelerating and the platform scales efficiently, forward FCF could reach ~$5,800M. At a growth-justified 38–40x multiple, the forward market cap could exceed $220B, well above current levels.

## Bear Case
The stock is already down ~19% YTD despite blowout results, signaling market skepticism on valuation sustainability. Persistent short-seller overhang (CapitalWatch allegations), key-person transitions (CTO and Chief Legal Officer changes), and potential margin compression as the platform scales to new advertiser types all pose risks. If growth decelerates meaningfully and the multiple compresses toward the 3-year average (~31x), forward FCF of ~$4,800M would imply a market cap closer to ~$134B, representing significant downside from current levels.

## Logic
- **Forward FCF estimate:** TTM FCF is $4,430.8M. Q1 2026 alone generated ~$1.3B FCF on $1.84B revenue. Annualizing Q1 run-rate (~$5.2B) and layering continued growth from Q2 guidance ($1.93B revenue midpoint) plus platform expansion, I estimate forward 12-month FCF at ~$5,400M — reflecting ~22% growth over TTM, a deceleration from the 75% YoY pace but still robust.
- **Applied EV/FCF multiple:** Current EV/FCF is ~40.2x. The 3-year average yield (0.0317) implies ~31.5x. Given the strong growth profile but real risk overhangs (short-seller allegations, leadership transitions, valuation concerns), I apply a blended 34.0x — below current but above the 3-year average, balancing growth against uncertainty.
- **EV → Market cap bridge:** Current EV − MC gap is $755.4M (net debt). Applying the same gap: Forward EV = 5,400 × 34.0 = $183,600M; Forward MC = $183,600 − $755.4 ≈ $182,845M.

## Bull Case
AppLovin's Q1 2026 results were exceptional: 59% revenue growth, 109% net income growth, 85% adjusted EBITDA margins, and ~$1.3B in quarterly FCF. The June 2026 public launch of AppLovin Ads dramatically expands the addressable advertiser base after 14 years of closed access, potentially unlocking a new growth leg beyond mobile gaming. TTM FCF of $4.43B grew 75% YoY, and Q2 guidance implies continued momentum. The self-serve platform could accelerate advertiser onboarding with minimal marginal cost, supporting sustained high FCF conversion. Even at the current ~40x EV/FCF, if forward FCF reaches $5.7B+ and the multiple holds, meaningful upside exists.

## Bear Case
The stock is down ~19% YTD despite blowout results, signaling market skepticism around valuation sustainability. Short-seller allegations (CapitalWatch), compliance concerns, and key-person transitions (CTO and CAO both changing in summer 2026) add execution risk. An EV/FCF of ~40x is demanding even for this growth profile; any deceleration from the self-serve launch or macro softness could compress the multiple toward the 3-year average of ~31.5x. The platform expansion requires scaling infrastructure and support, which could pressure FCF margins in the near term.

## Logic
**Forward FCF:** TTM FCF is $4,430.8M. Q1 2026 alone generated ~$1.3B, implying a run-rate above TTM. Annualizing Q1 gives ~$5.2B; adding modest sequential growth through Q2 2027 (platform launch tailwind offset by some reinvestment) yields a forward FCF estimate of $5,700M (~29% growth over TTM, conservative vs. the 75% trailing growth).

**Applied Multiple:** Current EV/FCF is ~40.2x; 1-year average is ~46.6x; 3-year average is ~31.5x. Given continued hyper-growth but rising execution risk and YTD multiple compression, I apply 35.0x — below current but above the 3-year average.

**Forward EV:** $5,700M × 35.0 = $199,500M

**EV-to-MC Bridge:** Current EV − MC gap = $178,125.0M − $177,369.6M = $755.4M (net debt). Applying the same gap: Forward MC = $199,500M − $755.4M = $198,744.6M.
